content.text:
I fixed the bug with a small change in `src/Tokenizer.ts`. I haven't run anything: the folder has no `node_modules`, so neither the test suite nor the example from the report has been checked against the change.

**Cause:** `outputLink()` handles both links and images. Before parsing the bracketed text it sets `lexer.state.inLink = true`, and afterwards it set it back to `false` no matter what it was before. The image `![logo](logo.png)` is parsed inside the outer link's text, so when it finished it cleared the flag while the outer link was still being parsed. The GFM bare-URL check (`!this.state.inLink && this.tokenizer.url(src)` in `src/Lexer.ts:511`) then treated `www.example.com` as being outside a link and made it a second, nested link.

**Fix:** `outputLink()` now saves the previous `inLink` value and restores it afterwards instead of resetting it to `false`. Once the image is done, the flag is still `true`, so the text after it stays plain text inside the outer link. This is the same save-and-restore pattern the function already uses for `linkEmitted` and `inRawBlock`.

The `www.`, `https://` and email cases all go through that same bare-URL check. Reference-style links and images also go through `outputLink()`, so they are covered by the same fix. Outside a link nothing changes, because the saved value there is `false`, the same value the old code set.
